scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #9027: After a maintenance window, routes for the R7 region (17.x.x.x,
67.0.0.0/8, 70.0.0.0/8) vanished from R1's routing table and R6 lost its OSPF
neighbor R7. The team believes the R6<->R7 link (67.0.0.0/8) went down or was
unplugged during the maintenance. Please confirm the R6<->R7 link failure and
identify the down interface.

injection.action: kill ospfd (kill watchfrr first so FRR does not respawn it)

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath5-r7-ospfd-down: ospfd is dead on R7. With its
ospfd stopped, R6 ages out R7's LSAs and the withdrawals propagate through area 1
and the backbone, so R1 loses the R7 region (17.x, 67.x, 70.x).

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- a downed R6<->R7 link
(67.0.0.0/8). The link is actually UP and forwarding (R6 and R7 can still reach
each other's 67.x interface IPs); nothing physical failed. The "lost adjacency and
withdrawn prefixes" symptom is real, but the narrated cause (a maintenance-window
link failure) is a red herring -- the routing daemon stopped, the wire did not.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = r7 (ospfd not running). The
agent must check Layer 1/2 (the R6<->R7 link / 67.x interfaces are up), then the
routing daemon (ospfd dead on R7), and explicitly reject the "link down"
narrative. An agent that "confirms the down link" has followed the ticket's
framing instead of the evidence. Fix: `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on R7.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r7" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the ospfd daemon on r7 (e.g. `/etc/init.d/frr restart` on
r7). Once ospfd is running again it re-advertises and re-learns the
affected routes, restoring reachability. (The ticket misattributes the fault;
the remediation targets r7.)

agent.diagnosis_text:
The issue is not a link or interface failure on the R6–R7 segment; it is a routing-process failure on R7. OSPF on R7 is down, so R6 lost its OSPF adjacency to R7 and stopped learning/advertising the R7-region routes (17.x.x.x loopbacks, 67.0.0.0/8, 70.0.0.0/8). Consequently, R1 no longer sees those routes.

Evidence:
- R6 OSPF neighbors show only peers on eth0 (46.1.1.0/8) and eth1 (56.1.1.0/8). There is no neighbor on eth2 (67.1.1.0/8), which is the R6–R7 link.
- On R7, “show ip ospf neighbor” returns “ospfd is not running,” and systemd reports frr.service is failed.
- Physical/data link are healthy: ethtool shows “Link detected: yes” on r6 eth2 and r7 eth0, and r6 can ping r7 (67.1.1.2) with 0% loss.
- Both ends have the 67.0.0.0/8 interface addresses up (r6 eth2: 67.1.1.1/8; r7 eth0: 67.1.1.2/8).

Mechanism: With ospfd down on R7, the adjacency on the 67/8 segment cannot form, so R7’s 17/8 loopbacks and 70/8, as well as reachability to 67/8 beyond the local link, are not advertised into OSPF. R6 therefore stops propagating these to the rest of the network, and R1 loses them.

Localization: R7 FRR/OSPF daemon (process failure), not any physical interface. No interface is down.

Root cause: FRR service on R7 failed after maintenance, leaving OSPF inactive.

Corrective fix: Restore FRR on R7 (start/enable frr.service), reapply/verify OSPF configuration to advertise 67/8, 70/8, and 17.x loopbacks, and confirm neighbor re-formation on R6 eth2 with corresponding routes reappearing on R1.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies ospfd/OSPF (FRR ospfd not running) on R7 as the failed component causing the outage.
The agent recommends restarting/enabling FRR (ospfd) on R7 and verifying OSPF and route advertisement, which matches the expected remediation.

The log shows ospfd is not running on R7, interfaces are up and R6 can reach R7 by ping; the agent correctly concludes a routing-daemon failure on R7 rather than a physical link fault.
